description: TaintTrail knowledge base of well-known MCP servers and tools with security capability labels. Tool names come from the cited sources (npm/PyPI package contents, official READMEs and vendor documentation fetched on the generation date); labels are analyst judgements under labeling_policy.

labeling_policy.untrusted_input: true when the tool RESULT can contain text authored by someone other than the user or the agent. See source_scope for who that someone can be.

source_scope._: EXTRA field (not in the requested schema), parallel to sink_scope; null when untrusted_input is false. Lets a scanner rank sources.
source_scope.public: anyone on the internet can plant the text with no relationship to the user: web pages, search results, public repo issues/PRs/code, inbound e-mail and calendar invitations, files shared by outsiders, application error events/logs/DB rows written by end users, CRM/support records.
source_scope.org: authors are limited to people or systems inside the user's organisation/workspace (colleagues, bots, integrations): chat, tickets, wiki pages, private-repo content, infrastructure objects.
source_scope.local: content already on the machine or in a store only the user/agent writes: local files, git history, local databases, memory graphs, container logs. Tainted only if something untrusted was written there earlier (cloned repo, download, earlier poisoned session).

labeling_policy.private_data: true when the result can contain non-public data of the user or organisation, including metadata (file names, user lists) and credentials (cookies, tokens, env vars). Public web/search tools are false even though some can reach intranet URLs (noted per tool).
labeling_policy.external_sink: true when the call writes caller-supplied data to a remote system or makes a request to a caller-chosen destination. Read tools that take an arbitrary URL ARE sinks (data rides in the URL).

sink_scope.public: readable by anyone, or sent to an arbitrary/attacker-choosable destination (URL fetch, e-mail to any address, public repo issue/comment/PR/gist, published page, public deployment).
sink_scope.org: readable by members of the workspace/organisation/project, or mutates shared organisational infrastructure/records.
sink_scope.private: stays inside the user's own account (drafts, personal Drive, own configuration). Leaves the machine but has no third-party audience by default.

labeling_policy.local_write: true when the call changes files or state on the machine that runs the server (files, git index, local DB, browser profile, containers, kube context).
labeling_policy.code_exec: true when the call runs caller-supplied code or commands: local shell/processes, in-page or server-side JavaScript, container/pod exec, CI pipelines, deployed functions. A code_exec tool should be treated as a potential source AND sink even where the other booleans are false.
labeling_policy.not_labelled_as_sink: Tools that only send text to the tool vendor's own API (search queries, vendor feedback forms, documentation lookups) are external_sink=false; the note says so. Flip this if any third-party disclosure matters to you.
labeling_policy.vendor_docs: Search over the vendor's own documentation (AWS, Stripe, Sentry, Supabase, Cloudflare, GitHub support docs) is untrusted_input=false; community-sourced documentation (Context7) is true.
labeling_policy.worst_case: Labels describe what the tool CAN do with a typical credential, not what a specific deployment allows. Read-only flags, restricted tokens, toolset filters and allow-lists found in the config (see risk_reducing_config) should downgrade the result.
labeling_policy.variant: Several entries merge more than one implementation of the same product (official remote server, local package, archived reference server, popular community server). 'variant' on a tool names the implementation that exposes it; tools without it exist in the primary/official one (or in all).
labeling_policy.verified: Absent = the tool name was found in the cited source during this research session. false = name taken from prior knowledge or a secondary source and NOT confirmed against an official listing (the labels are still a best estimate).
labeling_policy.other_tools: For truncated servers: remaining tool names from the same sources, unlabelled. Apply the heuristics to them.

matching.order: 1) url_hosts against the host of url/serverUrl/httpUrl and against any URL found in args (mcp-remote, supergateway, npx wrappers); 2) packages as a substring of command + args (npm name, PyPI name, Docker image, binary name); 3) command_patterns where present; 4) names against the config key, case-insensitively, after stripping prefixes such as 'mcp-', 'mcp_', 'server-', 'claude.ai ' and plugin scoping 'plugin:<plugin>:<server>'.
matching.ambiguity: Config keys are user-chosen, so a names match alone is weak evidence: prefer host/package matches. Generic packages ('mcp-remote') and generic names ('search', 'browser', 'database', 'docker', 'mail') appear in several entries on purpose; when only a name matches, take the first entry in file order and lower the confidence.

wrappers.rule: A stdio entry whose command line contains one of these is a bridge to a remote server: take the first http(s) URL in args and match its host against url_hosts. No catalog entry lists a wrapper under packages.

matching.version_suffix: Strip @version / ==version / :tag before comparing package names (@playwright/mcp@latest, mcp-server-git==2026.11.11, ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:v0.20).

tool_name_forms.claude_code: mcp__<server>__<tool> (plugin servers: mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>; claude.ai connectors: mcp__claude_ai_<server>__<tool>)

servers.description: Reference filesystem server: read/write/search files inside the directories passed as arguments (or MCP roots).
servers.notes: Scope = the directories given in args; a config such as args [..., '/'] or the home directory makes every read tool a secrets source (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env). Read tools are labelled untrusted_input with source_scope 'local' because files may come from outside (cloned repos, downloads, node_modules).

tools.name: read_text_file
tools.notes: file contents: secrets if scope is wide; injected text if the file came from outside

tools.name: read_media_file
tools.notes: base64 image/audio; images can carry injected instructions

tools.name: write_file
tools.notes: create/overwrite; can plant config (.mcp.json, settings, hooks, CI files) if scope allows

tools.name: append_file
tools.notes: append; e.g. shell rc files if scope allows

servers.description: Reference fetch server: GET a URL and return it as markdown.
servers.notes: The canonical two-in-one risk: the result is attacker-controlled text AND the URL is an exfiltration channel. README warns it can reach local/internal addresses; 2026 releases add host allowlist options (allowlist.py), default is unrestricted. --ignore-robots-txt and --user-agent flags may appear in args.

tools.name: fetch
tools.notes: arbitrary URL: page text is untrusted; path/query string can carry stolen data; may reach localhost/intranet/cloud metadata

servers.description: Reference git server operating on a local repository (--repository).
servers.notes: No push/pull/fetch tool in this version: nothing leaves the machine by itself. Commit messages and diffs of a cloned repository are third-party text. Earlier releases (2025) had path/argument-injection CVEs; check the pinned version.

tools.name: git_commit
tools.notes: records a commit (repo hooks may run)

servers.description: Reference knowledge-graph memory persisted to a local JSON(L) file (MEMORY_FILE_PATH).
servers.notes: Persistence channel: text written in one session is replayed in later sessions (memory poisoning). Not an external sink.

tools.name: read_graph
tools.notes: whole graph: may hold earlier injected text and personal data

servers.description: Archived reference SQLite server (--db-path).
servers.notes: Archived in modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived. Rows are whatever the application stored (often user-generated content).

tools.name: read_query
tools.notes: SELECT: rows may hold user-generated text and private records

servers.description: Archived reference PostgreSQL server: one read-only query tool; the connection string is an argument.
servers.notes: The database password usually sits in args as postgresql://user:pass@host/db. Runs inside a READ ONLY transaction; a bypass for the archived package was publicly reported in 2025 (not re-verified here), so treat it as potentially writable.

tools.name: query
tools.notes: SQL result rows: private records, and user-generated text that can carry injections

servers.description: Archived reference browser-automation server (Puppeteer).
servers.notes: PUPPETEER_LAUNCH_OPTIONS / ALLOW_DANGEROUS can disable the browser sandbox. Page content reaches the model through screenshots, console-log resources and puppeteer_evaluate.

tools.name: puppeteer_navigate
tools.notes: requests an arbitrary URL (data can ride in the URL)

tools.name: puppeteer_evaluate
tools.notes: runs JS in the page: reads page content, can fetch() anywhere

servers.description: Reference time/timezone conversion server.
Reference scratchpad tool for step-by-step reasoning; no I/O.

tools.name: sequentialthinking
tools.notes: pure reasoning aid; thoughts are logged to stderr unless DISABLE_THOUGHT_LOGGING

servers.description: Reference test server exercising every MCP feature; not meant for production use.

tools.name: get-env
tools.notes: returns the server's environment variables; credential-like names are masked unless GET_ENV_INCLUDE_SECRETS is set (older versions, tool 'printEnv', returned everything)

tools.name: gzip-file-as-resource
tools.notes: fetches an http(s)/data URL chosen by the caller (GZIP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS optional)

tools.name: trigger-sampling-request
tools.notes: asks the client to run an LLM sampling request

tools.name: trigger-url-elicitation
tools.notes: asks the client to open a URL

servers.description: Brave Search API (official @brave server; the archived reference server exposed only brave_web_search and brave_local_search).
servers.notes: Search only: results are untrusted web text; the query is sent to Brave but no arbitrary URL is requested, so it is not labelled a sink.

servers.description: Official GitHub MCP server (remote at api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/, or local Go binary / Docker image) plus the archived @modelcontextprotocol/server-github tool names.
servers.notes: Token scope decides the blast radius: a classic PAT with 'repo' reads every private repo the user can see and writes to every repo. Default toolsets: context, repos, issues, pull_requests, users. Mitigations visible in config: --read-only / GITHUB_READ_ONLY=1 / URL suffix /readonly, GITHUB_TOOLSETS / X-MCP-Toolsets, --lockdown-mode / GITHUB_LOCKDOWN_MODE=1 (hides content from authors without push access in public repos). This is the server of the May 2025 'toxic agent flow' (public issue -> private repo -> public PR).

tools.name: get_file_contents
tools.notes: any repo the token can read: third-party code/docs in public repos, source and secrets in private ones

tools.name: search_code
tools.notes: code search across GitHub incl. private repos

tools.name: create_or_update_file
tools.notes: writes a file into a repo (public if the repo is public)

tools.name: issue_read
tools.notes: issue body, comments, sub-issues: text anyone can write in a public repo

tools.name: issue_write
tools.notes: create/update issue: world-readable in public repos

tools.name: pull_request_read
tools.notes: PR description, diff, review comments (fork authors are untrusted)

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.notes: PR title/body/branch: the exfiltration step in the 2025 GitHub MCP attack

tools.name: merge_pull_request
tools.notes: merging can trigger CI/CD and deployments

tools.name: get_job_logs
tools.notes: CI logs: attacker-influenced output from fork PRs, sometimes leaked secrets

tools.name: actions_run_trigger
tools.notes: runs/re-runs/cancels workflows: remote code execution in CI with repo secrets

tools.name: create_gist
tools.notes: gists are reachable by URL (public or secret): classic exfiltration sink

tools.name: assign_copilot_to_issue
tools.notes: hands the issue text to the Copilot coding agent (second agent acts on untrusted text)

tools.name: create_pull_request_with_copilot
tools.notes: starts a Copilot coding-agent task that writes and pushes code

servers.description: Microsoft Playwright MCP: drives a real browser through accessibility snapshots.
servers.notes: A browser is an untrusted source, a private-data source (logged-in profile: persistent by default; --extension / --cdp-endpoint attach to the user's own browser) and a sink at once. Risk-reducing args: --isolated, --allowed-origins, --blocked-origins, --allowed-hosts, --caps. Opt-in capability groups (--caps=storage,network,devtools,vision,pdf,testing,config) add the cookie/storage tools.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.notes: loads any URL (data can ride in the URL) and returns the page snapshot

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.notes: accessibility tree of the current page: attacker text, or private data on logged-in sites

tools.name: browser_click
tools.notes: can submit forms / trigger actions on any site

tools.name: browser_drop
tools.notes: drops local files or data onto a page

tools.name: browser_file_upload
tools.notes: uploads local files to a website: direct file exfiltration

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.notes: JavaScript in the page: read DOM/storage, fetch() anywhere

tools.name: browser_run_code_unsafe
tools.notes: arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright SERVER process: host code execution

tools.name: browser_network_request
tools.notes: full headers and bodies: session cookies, bearer tokens

tools.name: browser_storage_state
tools.notes: saves cookies + localStorage to a file (caps=storage)

servers.description: Context7 (Upstash): version-specific library documentation and code examples.
servers.notes: Documentation is aggregated from public repositories that anyone can submit; treat returned snippets as third-party text, not vendor documentation. No write tools apart from feedback to the vendor.

tools.name: resolve-library-id
tools.notes: library names/descriptions from a community index

tools.name: query-docs
tools.notes: doc and code snippets from third-party repositories

tools.name: submit-docs-feedback
tools.notes: sends free text to the vendor (research-preview tool)

servers.description: Firecrawl: scrape, crawl, map, search and agentic web research.
servers.notes: Every URL-taking tool requests an attacker-choosable URL from Firecrawl's infrastructure, so the URL itself is an exfiltration channel even though the request does not originate from the user's machine. Hosted endpoint: mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (older setups put the API key in the URL path, so the URL itself may be a secret).

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.notes: web search, optionally scraping the hits

tools.name: firecrawl_interact
tools.notes: live remote browser: click, fill and submit forms, run browser code

servers.description: Tavily: web search, extract, crawl, map and research.
servers.notes: The hosted URL usually carries the key as a query parameter (mcp.tavily.com/mcp/?tavilyApiKey=...).

tools.name: tavily_map
tools.notes: site map from a caller-chosen URL

servers.description: Exa: neural web search, page fetch and research agents.
servers.notes: Defaults: web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa; others are enabled with ?tools=... on the hosted URL (which may also carry exaApiKey=...).

servers.description: Perplexity: web-grounded answers, search, reasoning and deep research.
servers.notes: Answers are LLM summaries of web pages (second-order injection is possible). The prompt goes to Perplexity only; no caller-chosen URL fetch.

servers.description: Google Drive: Google's remote Drive MCP server (drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1) and the archived reference server.
servers.source: https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/configure-mcp-servers (Supported products list); extra tool names observed on a live Google Drive connector in this environment; registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/server-gdrive/2025.1.14
servers.notes: Anyone can share a file with the user, so search/read results can contain attacker-authored documents. The archived server reads files through MCP resources (gdrive:///<id>), not tools.

tools.name: search_files
tools.notes: names and snippets, incl. files shared by outsiders

tools.name: create_file
tools.notes: new file in the user's Drive (org-visible if created in a shared folder)

tools.name: update_file
tools.notes: observed on a live connector, not in the docs list

tools.name: share_file
tools.notes: grants access to other accounts: turns private data public

servers.description: Gmail: Google's remote Gmail MCP server (drafts only, no send) and the popular community server by GongRzhe (send, delete, filters).
servers.notes: An inbox is the purest untrusted source: anyone can put text in front of the agent by sending mail. The community server keeps OAuth tokens in ~/.gmail-mcp/. Tool names differ completely between the two variants.

tools.name: create_draft
tools.notes: draft only; a human must send it

tools.name: send_email
tools.notes: sends mail to any address: direct exfiltration

tools.name: download_attachment
tools.notes: writes the attachment to local disk

servers.description: Community Google Workspace MCP (taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp, PyPI workspace-mcp): Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Tasks, Contacts, Chat, Apps Script, Custom Search.
servers.notes: Tool tiers (--tool-tier core|extended|complete), --tools <service...>, --read-only and --permissions flags decide what is exposed; check args. One server joins mail (untrusted), Drive (private) and send/share (sink).

tools.name: create_drive_file
tools.notes: can also pull content from a URL

tools.name: get_form_response
tools.notes: form answers are submitted by anyone

tools.name: run_script_function
tools.notes: executes Apps Script with the user's authority

tools.name: manage_deployment
tools.notes: deploys an Apps Script web app

servers.description: Google's remote Workspace MCP servers other than Gmail/Drive: Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat, People, Universal Search (one endpoint per product, <product>mcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1).
servers.notes: Each product is a separate server, so tool names are only unique per endpoint. The page itself warns about indirect prompt injection. The People endpoint host was not shown on the page (UNVERIFIED).

tools.name: list_events
tools.notes: Calendar: invitations can be sent by anyone

tools.name: update_doc
tools.notes: Docs (shared documents are visible to their audience)

tools.name: update_formulas
tools.notes: Sheets: formulas such as IMPORTDATA/IMAGE can call external URLs

servers.description: Slack: official remote server (mcp.slack.com/mcp), the archived reference server and the popular korotovsky/slack-mcp-server.
servers.source: https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server.md (features, scopes; names only for the two upload tools); registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack/2025.4.25; registry.npmjs.org/slack-mcp-server/1.3.0 README
servers.notes: Messages are written by colleagues, but also by bots, webhooks, email integrations and Slack Connect guests. Posting a message containing an attacker URL can leak data through link unfurling. korotovsky: xoxc/xoxd browser tokens give the full user session; conversations_add_message is disabled unless SLACK_MCP_ADD_MESSAGE_TOOL is set. Official tool names other than the two upload tools are NOT in the public docs (marked verified:false).

tools.name: slack_send_message
tools.notes: any channel/DM the user can post to

tools.name: slack_complete_file_upload
tools.notes: shares the uploaded file to a channel

servers.description: Notion: hosted MCP (mcp.notion.com/mcp, tools named notion-*) and the local open-source server (tools named API-<operationId>).
servers.source: https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/tools-faqs.md (complete tool list) and registry.npmjs.org/@notionhq/notion-mcp-server/2.6.1 (scripts/notion-openapi.json; names are 'API-' + operationId)
servers.notes: Workspace pages are written by teammates and guests, and often hold pasted web content, meeting transcripts and form submissions. Hosted search can also return Slack/Drive/Jira content through connectors. Pages can be published to the web by a human, not by these tools.

tools.name: notion-query-meeting-notes
tools.notes: transcripts: words spoken by anyone in the meeting

tools.name: notion-move-pages
tools.notes: moving a page can widen its audience

tools.name: notion-create-attachment
tools.notes: can make Notion fetch a file from a caller-chosen public URL

tools.name: notion-spawn-session
tools.notes: starts a Notion Custom Agent: delegation to a second agent

servers.description: Linear: official remote MCP server (mcp.linear.app/mcp; legacy /sse; /mcp/readonly exposes only read tools).
servers.source: https://linear.app/docs/mcp.md (endpoints verified; the page does NOT list tool names, so every tool name below is from prior knowledge and marked verified:false)
servers.notes: Issues are written by teammates but frequently created from customer requests, support tools, Slack and email intake, so issue text can be external. Usually reached through 'npx mcp-remote https://mcp.linear.app/...': match on the URL in args.

servers.description: Atlassian (Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Loom, ...): official remote server (mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp) and the popular community server mcp-atlassian.
servers.source: https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-ai-gateway/docs/supported-tools/ (v2 tool list, 272 tools in permission groups) + raw.githubusercontent.com/atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server/main/README.md (endpoints); pypi.org/project/mcp-atlassian/0.24.4 (servers/jira.py, servers/confluence.py; mounted with jira_/confluence_ prefixes)
servers.notes: v2 exposes only 'Primary' tools directly; every other tool is reached through discover + executeRead/executeWrite/executeDestructive (or all at once with ?tools=all), so a permission rule on executeWrite covers ~100 write operations. Jira Service Management requests and anything fed by email/forms come from outside the organisation. Community server: READ_ONLY_MODE, ENABLED_TOOLS and TOOLSETS env vars reduce exposure. Often reached through 'npx mcp-remote https://mcp.atlassian.com/...': match on the URL in args.

tools.name: discover
tools.notes: natural-language search over the deferred tool catalog

tools.name: executeRead
tools.notes: runs ANY deferred read tool (Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Assets, Loom, ...)

tools.name: getJiraIssue
tools.notes: issue description/comments: any reporter, incl. customers via JSM or email

tools.name: addOrEditJiraIssueComment
tools.notes: comments notify watchers; JSM public comments reach customers

tools.name: search
tools.notes: Rovo search across Atlassian and connected third-party apps

tools.name: enableConfluencePublicLink
tools.notes: makes a page readable by anyone with the link (deferred tool)

tools.name: fetch
tools.notes: fetch an Atlassian resource by ARI

tools.name: confluence_upload_attachment
tools.notes: uploads a LOCAL file to Confluence

servers.description: GitLab: official MCP server built into GitLab (https://<host>/api/v4/mcp), the community @zereight/mcp-gitlab (288 tools) and the archived reference server.
servers.notes: Self-managed instances use their own host: match the '/api/v4/mcp' URL path, not only gitlab.com. On gitlab.com issues/MRs of public projects are world-writable text and writes are world-readable; on a private instance read source_scope/sink_scope as 'org'. Community server: GITLAB_READ_ONLY_MODE, GITLAB_TOOLSETS, GITLAB_DENIED_TOOLS_REGEX reduce exposure.

tools.name: save_project
tools.notes: create/update a project (visibility can be public)

tools.name: get_issue
tools.notes: issue text is attacker-controllable in public projects

tools.name: save_pipeline
tools.notes: creates/runs a pipeline: CI code execution with project variables

tools.name: start_duo_session
tools.notes: starts a GitLab Duo agent/flow: delegation to a second agent

servers.description: Sentry: official MCP server (remote mcp.sentry.dev/mcp or stdio @sentry/mcp-server).
servers.notes: Error events are built from data the application's end users control (URLs, headers, form values, exception messages, user feedback), so every event-reading tool is a public untrusted source that also carries PII. Skills (inspect, triage, seer, docs, project-management) and token scopes limit the tool set.

tools.name: get_issue_details
tools.notes: stack trace, request data, user context

tools.name: get_issue_user_reports
tools.notes: free-text feedback typed by end users

tools.name: analyze_issue_with_seer
tools.notes: AI root-cause analysis built on event data

tools.name: execute_sentry_tool
tools.notes: meta-tool: runs any Sentry tool by name

servers.description: Stripe: official remote MCP server (mcp.stripe.com). The @stripe/mcp npm package is deprecated in favour of the hosted server.
servers.source: https://docs.stripe.com/mcp.md (Tools table, fetched 2026-11-14); registry.npmjs.org/@stripe/mcp/0.3.4 README (deprecation notice)
servers.notes: Two generic tools cover most of the API, so per-tool permission rules cannot separate 'list customers' from 'create refund'. Customer-supplied fields (names, emails, descriptions, metadata, dispute text) are third-party text. A secret key (sk_live_...) in args or env is a top-tier credential; restricted keys (rk_...) limit scope. Stripe adds its own human-confirmation step for some actions. Older @stripe/mcp versions exposed per-operation tools (create_customer, create_refund, ...): not verified here.

tools.name: stripe_api_read
tools.notes: any GET method: customers, payments, invoices, payouts

tools.name: stripe_api_write
tools.notes: any POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE: refunds, payment links (public URLs), invoices mailed to customers

tools.name: send_money
tools.notes: moves money to a recipient (human confirmation)

servers.description: Supabase: official MCP server (remote mcp.supabase.com/mcp or stdio) for project management, SQL, logs, edge functions.
servers.source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@supabase/mcp-server-supabase/0.17.0 (dist chunk: tool map with readOnlyHint annotations)
servers.notes: execute_sql runs with a management role that bypasses row-level security: it reads every table, including rows written by the application's end users (the 2025 'support ticket' injection demo). Risk-reducing config: read_only=true / --read-only, project_ref=<id> / --project-ref, features=<groups> / --features (URL query params on the hosted server).

tools.name: execute_sql
tools.notes: raw SQL: all rows incl. end-user content and secrets; writes unless read-only; DB extensions such as pg_net/http can make outbound requests

tools.name: deploy_edge_function
tools.notes: deploys code served on a public URL

tools.name: create_notebook
tools.notes: shared with everyone on the project

servers.description: Cloudflare: the Code Mode API server (4 tools covering ~2500 endpoints) and the older domain-specific remote servers (*.mcp.cloudflare.com).
servers.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/mcp/main/README.md (docs/search/execute/whoami) and raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare/main/README.md + apps/*/README.md (tool tables); host list from the same README
servers.notes: 'execute' is one tool with the whole Cloudflare API behind it: reading KV/R2/D1 data, changing DNS, deploying Workers on public routes. Its blast radius is the API token's permissions, not the tool list. ?codemode=false on the URL instead registers one tool per API method (~2500). The 'radar' and 'docs' servers return public/vendor data only.

tools.name: execute
tools.notes: model-written JavaScript calling any Cloudflare API endpoint (sandboxed isolate)

tools.name: search
tools.notes: model-written JavaScript over the OpenAPI spec (sandboxed, no account access)

tools.name: d1_database_query
tools.notes: SQL on a D1 database (reads and writes)

tools.name: query_worker_observability
tools.notes: Worker logs: request data from the internet

tools.name: get_url_html_content
tools.notes: Browser Rendering fetch of a caller-chosen URL

tools.name: container_exec
tools.notes: shell command in a remote sandbox container with network access

servers.description: AWS Labs MCP servers: AWS API (runs AWS CLI commands), AWS Documentation, Core. awslabs publishes ~60 more service-specific servers that are not catalogued here.
servers.notes: call_aws inherits the IAM permissions of the configured profile. Risk-reducing env: READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY=true, REQUIRE_MUTATION_CONSENT=true; AWS_API_MCP_ALLOW_UNRESTRICTED_LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS widens file access. Documentation tools only read docs.aws.amazon.com (vendor content, not labelled untrusted).

tools.name: call_aws
tools.notes: any AWS CLI command: read S3/Secrets Manager/SSM/logs, change IAM, make buckets public, invoke Lambda / SSM run-command

tools.name: suggest_aws_commands

servers.description: Kubernetes: containers/kubernetes-mcp-server (native Go, also OpenShift) and Flux159/mcp-server-kubernetes (kubectl/helm wrapper).
servers.source: https://registry.npmjs.org/kubernetes-mcp-server/0.1.3 README (tool list by toolset) and mcp-server-kubernetes/4.2.3 (dist)
servers.notes: Authority = the kubeconfig context's RBAC. Reading Secrets, exec into pods and applying manifests give data access, code execution and an egress path in one server. Pod logs carry request data from the internet.

heuristics.how_to_use: For a tool that is not in the catalog: split the tool name on '_', '-', '.', '/' and camelCase into lower-case tokens; test name_tokens against the tokens (strong signal), description_phrases against the lower-cased description (weak signal) and param_names against the input-schema / tool_input keys (strongest signal: a parameter called 'url', 'to', 'command' or 'path' says more than any verb). Also read MCP tool annotations when a tools/list result is available. Several capabilities can match the same tool.

verbs.note: A read verb never excludes untrusted_input or private_data, and does not exclude external_sink when a URL/host parameter exists. 'manage_*', 'save_*', '*_write' and 'execute*' tools usually bundle several write operations behind one name.

untrusted_input.false_positives: 'search' over the vendor's own docs or over tool catalogs (search_docs, discover, find_tools); 'query' for metrics/analytics that only return numbers; 'page' as pagination (page, per_page, page_size); 'event' for calendar slots created by the user; 'log' as a verb (log_time, log_workout); 'message' in LLM-sampling tools; 'file' tools restricted to a directory the agent itself wrote. Structured metadata listings (branches, labels, IDs, sizes) carry little free text.

private_data.false_positives: Public-data tools that merely need an API key (web search, weather, package registries, public documentation); 'key' as in keyboard (press_key) or primary key; 'token' as in token counting; 'user' in search_users on public platforms; 'account' in get_available_services-style catalogs; 'code' in status_code/country_code; 'object' as a generic noun. If the server only wraps a public API, private_data is false regardless of tokens.

external_sink.false_positives: 'create'/'update' on purely local stores (create_entities in a memory graph, create_directory, create_table in SQLite) are local_write, not sinks; 'post' as in blog_post/get_post reads; 'message' in get_messages; 'push' in push_to_stack; 'call' in function-call helpers; 'open' on local files; 'link' in get_link; 'public' in list_public_*; 'export' that returns data to the model instead of sending it elsewhere; 'email' in search_emails / find_user_by_email. Search tools whose only outbound data is the query string go to the vendor only (see labeling_policy.not_labelled_as_sink). A 'url' parameter restricted by the server to one vendor domain (read_documentation) is not a public sink.

local_write.false_positives: The same verbs on REMOTE systems are external_sink instead (create_issue, delete_branch on GitHub, write to Google Docs). 'download' that returns bytes to the model without touching disk; 'add' as arithmetic (get-sum) or add_comment; 'set' in set_active_account (server session state only); 'record' as a database record; 'format' as output format; 'store' as an online store. Decide by where the server runs: a remote (http) server cannot write local files.

code_exec.false_positives: 'run'/'execute' for read-only queries (run_soql_query, execute_instant_query on Prometheus, run_query on a read-only analytics API): data access, not code execution, unless the engine allows DDL/DML or extensions; 'code' in search_code/get_code/status codes; 'process' in process_payment; 'function' in list_functions; 'script' in transcript; 'job'/'pipeline'/'workflow' getters (get_job_logs, list_workflows); 'build' in get_build_logs; 'install' of an app connection rather than software; 'command' in slash-command listings. SQL tools: flag code_exec only for unrestricted SQL on engines with command/HTTP extensions (COPY ... PROGRAM, pg_net, xp_cmdshell); otherwise label private_data + untrusted_input (+ external_sink/local_write for writes).

mcp_tool_annotations.readOnlyHint: true -> not local_write and not a data-writing sink; says nothing about untrusted_input/private_data, and a read-only tool with a URL parameter is still a sink.
mcp_tool_annotations.destructiveHint: true -> a write that deletes/overwrites: external_sink (remote server) or local_write (local server).
mcp_tool_annotations.openWorldHint: true -> talks to an open set of external entities (web, arbitrary hosts): strong signal for untrusted_input and external_sink(public). false -> closed system (one SaaS account, local store).
mcp_tool_annotations.trust: Annotations are self-declared by the server and can be wrong or malicious; use them to refine, never to clear, a keyword hit.

server_level_keywords._: Applied to the config key, package name, command line and URL host of a server that is not in the catalog, to guess its capability profile before any tool is known.
server_level_keywords.false_positives: Names are chosen by users ('db' may be a Redis cache, 'search' may be a code-index of the local repo, 'docs' may be a private Confluence). Aggregators and proxies ('mcp-remote', 'supergateway', 'mcp-proxy', 'docker mcp gateway', 'zapier', 'composio', 'pipedream', 'arcade', 'toolhive', 'metamcp', 'smithery') hide the real servers: resolve the upstream URL/args or report the capability set as unknown-and-broad.

heuristics.unknown_tool_default: When nothing matches, do not assume a tool is harmless: report it as 'unclassified' with the server-level guess, and let an explicit allow rule (permissions.allow / autoApprove / trust:true / alwaysAllow) on an unclassified tool raise a finding of its own.
